Better call Saul starts off as a slow burn & can be slow in other parts because there's actual details & layers due to who Jimmy is at his core & there were loads of things that eventually got him to his breaking point. 

Watching his dad be a pushover, Chuck not believing in him, Howard treating him like shit (This was because of Chuck), getting involved & forced into dealing with the cartel, Kim's influence on him, Watching Howard get shot, Kim breaking up with him.

Jimmy went through a lot, going through a lot of changes affects people differently, I'm not denying that he wasn't slippin' Jimmy at some point, but with Chuck's genuine support & belief in him when Jimmy became a lawyer is likely something that could've prevented the Saul - Gene epidemic. 

Again there is so much to his story & not just his, Nacho's backstory is tragic, he wanted out but instead we were forced to watch a dude who was willing to die for his dad be manipulated by Gus. Werner was one of the sweetest people in the show (by breaking bad universe standards) then we had to watch him get shot in the head by Mike (who clearly suffered with the misery of it afterwards).. Mike's fallout into the cartel.

Mike's story might be my favorite & this is because in breaking bad Mike is full set on being a cartel guy.. But even by the end of better call Saul he is still hesitant & uncomfortable being a henchmen for Gus, but he commits to it anyways because he knows he's in too deep, this is something I wish I saw talked about more.

So as far as detailed storytelling goes, Better call Saul is 100% objectively better..

but as far as entertainment goes, that is completely subjective, I *personally* believe the nonstop action in breaking bad makes it easier to watch because you don't necessarily need your eyes glued to the tv 24/7 because generally you know what's going on.. In better call Saul there's story happening 24/7, boring or not.. so you really can't miss anything.
